questions.stem: What quantity of electricity is passed when a current of 5.0 A flows for 10 minutes?
questions.explanation: Q = It requires the time in seconds, so 10 minutes becomes 10 x 60 = 600 s. Then Q = 5.0 x 600 = 3000 C. Using 10 rather than 600 would give an answer sixty times too small.

distractorRationale.a: The time was left in minutes, giving 5 x 10
distractorRationale.b: The current was omitted and only the time in seconds was quoted
distractorRationale.d: The Faraday constant was brought in, but it is not needed to find the charge

questions.stem: One faraday of electricity is the quantity of charge carried by
questions.explanation: A faraday is the charge on one mole of electrons, which is 96500 coulombs. It is the bridge between the electrical world of coulombs and the chemical world of moles, and it is why the half equation determines how much product a given charge yields.

distractorRationale.a: The charge on a single electron is about 1.6 x 10^-19 C, far smaller
distractorRationale.c: A coulomb is itself a unit of charge, so this statement is circular
distractorRationale.d: The charge depends on how many electrons are transferred, not on the amount of substance alone

questions.stem: What mass of silver is deposited when one faraday of electricity is passed through silver trioxonitrate(V) solution? [Ag = 108]
questions.explanation: The cathode half equation is Ag+ + e- -> Ag, so one mole of electrons deposits exactly one mole of silver. One faraday is one mole of electrons, and one mole of silver has a mass of 108 g.

distractorRationale.a: This assumes silver forms a 2+ ion needing two electrons, but silver is univalent
distractorRationale.c: This doubles the molar mass, as if one faraday deposited two moles
distractorRationale.d: This quotes the Faraday constant, which is a charge in coulombs, not a mass

questions.stem: A current of 2.0 A is passed through copper(II) sulphate solution for 30 minutes. What mass of copper is deposited at the cathode? [Cu = 64, 1 faraday = 96500 C]
questions.explanation: Q = 2.0 x 1800 = 3600 C. Since Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu, two faradays, that is 193000 C, deposit 64 g. So the mass is (3600 / 193000) x 64 = 230400 / 193000 = 1.19 g.

distractorRationale.a: The time was taken as 15 minutes, halving the charge
distractorRationale.c: The factor of two electrons per copper ion was omitted, using 96500 instead of 193000
distractorRationale.d: The molar mass was quoted as though a full two faradays had been passed

questions.stem: Calculate the quantity of electricity, in coulombs, passed when a current of 3.0 A flows for 5.0 minutes.
questions.explanation: Convert the time to seconds first: 5.0 x 60 = 300 s. Then Q = It = 3.0 x 300 = 900 C. Leaving the time in minutes would give 15 C, which is sixty times too small.

questions.stem: The same quantity of electricity is passed in series through a solution of silver trioxonitrate(V) and a solution of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI). Compared with the number of moles of copper deposited, the number of moles of silver deposited is
questions.explanation: Silver needs one electron per ion, Ag+ + e- -> Ag, while copper needs two, Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu. The same pool of electrons therefore discharges twice as many silver ions as copper ions. This is exactly what Faraday's second law describes.

distractorRationale.a: This reverses the relationship; the ion requiring fewer electrons is discharged in greater number
distractorRationale.b: Equal amounts would require the two ions to have the same charge, which they do not
distractorRationale.d: A factor of four would need copper to be Cu4+, which does not exist

questions.stem: What volume of oxygen, measured at s.t.p., is liberated at the anode when 9650 C of electricity is passed through acidified water? [1 faraday = 96500 C; molar volume = 22.4 dm3/mol]
questions.explanation: The anode reaction 4OH- -> 2H2O + O2 + 4e- needs four faradays, that is 386000 C, for one mole of oxygen. Moles of oxygen = 9650 / 386000 = 0.025 mol, and the volume is 0.025 x 22.4 = 0.56 dm3.

distractorRationale.a: Eight electrons per mole of oxygen were assumed instead of four
distractorRationale.c: Two electrons per mole of oxygen were used, which is the factor for hydrogen not oxygen
distractorRationale.d: One electron per mole of oxygen was assumed, ignoring the half equation entirely
